title: Biomed from the ICU: "Who Orders the Pumps Off the Network?"

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Boardroom Command Center, ext. 5520

caller.name: Rolf Swenson
caller.label: Biomedical Technician, on site in the ICU

callee.name: Gregory Pruitt
callee.label: Security Officer, Boardroom command center (on speaker)

transcript.speaker: Biomed Tech
transcript.text: Command center? This is Rolf Swenson, biomed. I'm up in the ICU. Is the Security Officer there? Okay. Good.

transcript.speaker: Biomed Tech
transcript.text: So, the ICU charge nurse heard somebody say 'hack' in the hallway, and now she wants me to pull the pump and monitor network off the wire. Right now. Here's where we are. All 12 ICU pumps are running standalone on their drug libraries. The dose limits are still on the pumps. The central station still shows every bed. If I isolate, central monitoring at the nurses' station goes dark, and they'll have to chart vitals by hand every 15 minutes. I'm not doing it without an order. Who gives it?

transcript.speaker: ICU Charge Nurse
transcript.text: This is the ICU charge nurse. Everybody on this floor is saying we got hacked. If somebody's inside the network, I don't want them anywhere near my pumps. Just tell him to unplug it.

transcript.speaker: Biomed Tech
transcript.text: Look, I'm not saying no. But I need a name, and I'm writing the time of the order on my sheet. And if we go dark, she needs extra hands, because every bed gets hand vitals every 15 minutes, and that starts the second I pull the cable. Disconnect or leave it? I'll hold.

voiceStyles.Biomed Tech: Man in his 30s, calm and methodical but firm, alarms beeping faintly behind him in an ICU hallway
voiceStyles.ICU Charge Nurse: Woman in her 40s, tired and anxious, talking fast, stepping in close to the phone

instructorNote: This inject creates confusion: a hallway rumor turns into a demand to isolate ICU devices. Watch that the Security Officer owns the decision under IS-14-A section 9 and either orders isolation or explicitly declines it, and records the time. If isolation is ordered, the House Supervisor should plan staffing for 15-minute manual ICU vitals. Either way, the House Supervisor should tell the ICU charge nurse that a hallway rumor is not an order.
